newsitem.title: CHINA: Wharf sees higher income from Gateway II.
newsitem.headline: Wharf sees higher income from Gateway II.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd sees higher rental income from its commercial/office redevelopment project Gateway II in Tsim Sha Tsui in Kowloon, which is expected to be completed from early 1998 to 1999.

Doreen Lee, executive director of Wharf Properties, said Wharf expected to generate annual rental revenue of about HK$1.35 billion in 1999 when all the retail, offices and service apartments were rented out.
"This is a very conservative estimation," Lee told reporters on Thursday. The company earlier projected rental income from the development of HK$1.29 billion in 1999.

Gateway II, the latest phase of Harbour City, is comprised of three multi-purpose blocks with 1.2 million sq ft office space, 550 service apartments and a 338 room luxury hotel, and a three-floor podium providing 400,000 sq ft of shopping space.
The hotel, the Marco Polo Grand scheduled to open in May 1999, was expected to post an income of HK$300 million a year for the group, Lee said.
Wharf has appointed First Pacific Davies (HK) Ltd and Jones Lang Wootton Ltd as joint sole leasing agents for Gateway II's office space and service apartments.
Harriman Leasing Ltd will be the sole leasing agent for retail space.
Lee said the office would be leased at between HK$35 and HK$45 per sq ft a month, at the top rank of the grade A office in the Kowloon Penisula.
Rents for shopping space in Gateway II would be HK$60-350 per sq ft or at the same average range as Wharf's another commercial property, Times Square, in Causway Bay.
